title: Heterogeneous Prefill/Decode Benchmark Conductor
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a reusable benchmark conductor that orchestrates heterogeneous workload sweeps across kernel candidates, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode pacing policies. The conductor should produce deterministic golden baselines, generate CI-friendly diffs, and surface model/hardware pair regressions at the token and tail-latency level.

Background: We frequently run ad-hoc experiments for kernel routing and prefill scheduling, but results are fragmented across scripts, different seed sets, and manual golden snapshots. This ticket consolidates those pieces into a single conductor that can: 1) schedule microbench and mixed-workload runs, 2) score kernel candidates with a stability-aware metric, 3) lock golden baselines and produce lockfile artifacts, 4) emit CI-ready comparisons and thresholded perf gates for presubmit checks.

Goals/Deliverables: Produce a v1 conductor binary and orchestration config, a standardized workload corpus (diverse lengths/cohorts), a golden lockfile format, a CI job that fails on >5% tail latency regression or >3% throughput drop, and documentation for engineering and bench owners.
tasks: Design conductor config schema and scoring function (owner: Rafael)
Compile standardized workload corpus with deterministic seeds and cohort labels (owner: Aisha)
Implement kernel candidate runner that accepts kernel matrix and returns per-token latency distributions (owner: Yun Li)
Integrate attention microbench (dense/sparse/multihead variants) into conductor (owner: Marco)
Add prefill pacing simulator and decode-concurrency sweeper (owner: Tiara)
Produce golden lockfile writer with signatures and provenance metadata (owner: Rafael)
Create CI job bench-compare that runs diff against golden lockfile and publishes failure reasons (owner: Infra)
Document runbook and add dashboard panels for tail quantiles and kernel-choice heatmap (owner: Aisha)
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can run mixed workloads end-to-end from config and produce a deterministic lockfile
Kernel scoring outputs top-3 candidates with stability score and per-quantile deltas
CI job bench-compare integrated in PR pipeline and can be toggled (on/off) per repo
Runbook and dashboard links present in ticket and validated by one platform engineer
Golden lockfile format accepted by runtime-1.20 release team and stored in s3://redwood-goldens/runtime-1.20/
progress_updates: 2025-01-10: Kickoff — scoped v1 features, aligned on metric: 95/99/999 quantiles + throughput + stability score (mean of bootstrapped samples).
2025-01-13: Design review — decided to encode kernel candidates as (kernel-id, flags, kernel-version) tuples to avoid name ambiguity. Rafael and Yun agreed on stable hash format for provenance.
2025-01-15: Prototype runner merged in branch feat/hetero-conductor (PR: https://github.com/redwood/benchmarks/pull/412). It supports single-model microbench and returns per-step latency histograms.

2025-01-17: Found trade-off — running full mixed-workload sweep increases CI runtime beyond budget. Decision: CI job will sample cohorts deterministically (seeded) and run a reduced sweep; full conductor runs scheduled nightly on bench infra.

2025-01-18: Added attention microbench for causal vs. block-sparse attention. Initial runs show block-sparse kernel reduces median latency on long contexts but increases short-context jitter — added stability penalty to scoring.
2025-01-20: Prefill pacing simulator implemented; discovered decode concurrency parameter interacts with KV cache warms — added warmup step to conductor and an option to lock prefill cache state.

2025-01-21: CI bench-compare prototype integrated into redwood/runtime repo as optional check (job: bench-compare-pr). First runs validated against golden snapshot from s3://redwood-goldens/runtime-1.20/seed-20250110.lock.
2025-01-22: UX review with console team — added requested JSON output with kernel-heatmap and quantile deltas for consumption by dashboards. Preparing docs for eng-oncall review.
notes: We intentionally bias scoring to penalize high-jitter kernels even if median improves — target is production reliability, not microbench peaks.
CI gate thresholds are configurable per project; runtime-1.20 will default to conservative thresholds for the first rollout.
Follow-up epic: expand corpus to include customer-derived workloads (sensitive data scrubber required)
